findings: FFR=0 VERIFIED: All 16 adversarial attack classes (red_safety_gate_report.md table) produce no false HIT. performance_validation.json reports frontend_false_reuse=0. Mutation suite (mutation_suite_results.json) confirms each of the 5 load-bearing legs is necessary: dropping L0/L1/L3/c4/extraction_params each produces a false HIT on at least one attack pair (produces_false_hit=true for all 5 mutations). total_tests=22, passed=22, failed=0, all_required_caught=true.

CFA=0 VERIFIED: c4 closure re-verification (certificate.py:416-435 verify_closure_content) re-reads every file in cached_entry.closure_file_list via Path(fpath).read_bytes() and re-hashes; any content change OR OSError (file deleted/unreadable) returns False -> safe MISS. Attacks #5 (transitive header), #6 (generated header same path new content), #7 (forced-include content change) are all caught by c4. performance_validation.json reports certificate_false_accept=0. Mutation drop_c4_closure produces_false_hit=true proves c4 is load-bearing. W1 negative control recorded 20 c4_rejections (bucket matched but closure differed) out of 25 TUs -- the gate actively fires.

GTP=0 VERIFIED: W2 positive control (per-file config) achieved 16 cache_hits / 9 actual_parses / 64% hit rate with correctness_pass=true and gt_parity_failures=0 in performance_validation.json. Reused ExtractionResult objects produce identical downstream facts to fresh parses (46969 symbols in W1, 17780 in W2, no parity divergence).

DEFAULT OFF VERIFIED: m9_reuse_enabled() (certificate.py:512-522) returns False unless FW_CONTEXT_M9_REUSE env var == '1'. The env read is un-cached so runtime toggling is honoured. The Tier 2.5 intercept (_unit_processor.py:326 'if m9_reuse_enabled():') and the cache-put path (_unit_processor.py:381 'if m9_reuse_enabled() and ...') are BOTH gated. When False, neither the bucket-key computation, cache lookup, nor cache put execute.

ZERO BEHAVIOR CHANGE WHEN DISABLED VERIFIED: certificate.py is imported at module level (_unit_processor.py:177-183) but the import is purely definitional -- only stdlib (hashlib/logging/os/threading/time/dataclasses/pathlib/typing) at module scope, no I/O, no env reads, no subprocess. All heavy imports (store_v2.certify, store_v2.ncc, indexer.macros) are lazy INSIDE compute_bucket_key/_compute_l3_with_env and thus never load when M9 is off. With the flag off, _check_and_parse_unit falls straight through to extract_all() at line 349 and returns ('updated', parsed, (t_parse_start, t_parse_end), hashes) -- byte-for-byte the pre-M9 path. The global cache (_GLOBAL_CACHE) is lazily initialised via get_certificate_cache() which is never called when disabled, so _GLOBAL_CACHE stays None (no memory cost).

CONSUMERS READ-ONLY VERIFIED: Comprehensive ripgrep across src/fw_context_mcp for parsed.<attr>=, del parsed.<attr>, parsed.<attr>.(append|extend|clear|pop|update|insert|remove)(, setattr(parsed, ...), parsed.tu.(reparse|save|parse|from_source), sym.<attr>=, result.<attr>= returned ZERO matches in store_v2/ and ops.py. Inspected all three consumers: (1) materialize_unit_into_m6 (m6_direct_materialization.py:48-256) reads parsed.symbols/call_sites/references/inheritance via getattr and iterates -- builds new payload dicts, never writes back. (2) certify_and_publish_for_unit (certify.py:1081-1200) calls build_certificate/extract_state_facts/build_cold_payload -- all read-only on parsed (sorted() returns a new list, no in-place mutation). (3) store_symbols_for_unit (ops.py:1549+) reads result.tu/symbols/references/inheritance/indirect_call_sites/fp_assignments/macros/pending_dispatches/call_sites/newly_seen_files via attribute access only. The cached CachedParse.parsed is therefore safe to hand to multiple TUs sequentially.

BUCKET KEY CAPTURES ALL SAFETY-CONTRACT INPUTS VERIFIED (certificate.py:236-331 compute_bucket_key): L0 = sha256(source_blob + unit.language + resolved-abs-main_file_path) -- catches source edits, #pragma pack, X-macro, __FILE__-dependent code, __COUNTER__ extra macro use. L1 = sha256(ncc_serial POST-class-C) -- canonical NCC argv ORDER-preserved, captures -D/-U/-I path AND order/-include/-std/--target/-m*/--resource-dir/--sysroot= (resource_dir confirmed caught via mutation_suite TestBuiltinMacros env_digest sensitivity + L1 argv capture). L3 = h('L3', toolchain_salt, parser_salt, '1', env_digest) where env_digest is the clang -dM -E builtin probe -- catches clang binary change, libclang version change, builtin macro changes, resource-dir affecting builtins. extraction_params = (frozenset(skip_files), with_refs) -- gap #1 closed; skip_files normalised to frozenset and sorted-repr'd in composition so set ordering is deterministic. Gap #2: -include-pch -> 'FORCE_MISS_PCH' sentinel (PCH is build-output). Three additional FORCE_MISS sentinels for unreadable source / NCC failure / L3 failure -- all fail-closed.

c4 CATCHES TRANSITIVE HEADER CHANGES VERIFIED: extract_closure_from_parsed (certificate.py:442-478) walks parsed.tu.get_includes() (same source as build_certificate's _closure_walk), dedups by absolute path, reads each file, hashes -- stores (file_list, content_hash) in the cache entry. On HIT, verify_closure_content re-reads the SAME file list and re-hashes. Because the closure_file_list captures ALL transitively-included files (including forced includes via -include, which appear in tu.get_includes() per attack #7), any transitive header content edit -- even with no macro/define change -- flips the hash and forces a safe MISS. The two-phase protocol (pre-parse bucket key + post-HIT c4 re-verification) correctly resolves the chicken-and-egg: c4 needs parsed.tu.get_includes() so it cannot be in the pre-parse bucket key, but the cached closure_file_list lets us re-verify cheaply (~0.5ms, file reads only) on HIT.

PERFORMANCE VALIDATED (performance_validation.json): W1 negative control (5 global-config builds, all TUs genuinely differ) -- 0 cache_hits, 25 misses, 20 c4_rejections, 1.55% wall-clock overhead (under 5% threshold). W2 positive control (per-file config, 5 builds sharing 16 TUs) -- 16 cache_hits, 9 actual_parses, 64% hit rate, 61.58% wall-time savings (exceeds 30% target). Certificate cost per TU: 0.0ms effective (cached L3 builtin probe). Avoided frontend cost: 40.6ms/TU. verdict.overall_pass=true.

DESIGN SOUNDNESS: The safety principle 'SAFE REUSE > MAXIMAL REUSE; false miss acceptable, false hit blocking' is consistently applied. Every uncertainty path (unreadable source, NCC failure, L3 failure, -include-pch, closure file unreadable) fails closed to MISS. The L3 two-level cache (_L3_BUILTIN_CACHE keyed by toolchain config only; _L3_FULL_CACHE keyed by (toolchain, ncc_serial)) is a pure performance optimisation that does not affect safety: the builtin probe cache is keyed by (libclang_id, cli_id, std_target_flags, target) which are all inputs the env_digest depends on, and the full cache's ncc_serial input captures the remaining argv variation.
